heading: CHAPTER XIX.
title: THAT ONE SHOULD AVOID BEING DESPISED AND HATED
exclusions: front matter and dedication before THE PRINCE
notes: Chapter 19 argues that a prince can survive many complaints but not the settled conditions of hatred and contempt, because those states invite conspiracy, weaken obedience, and turn shocks into political danger.
The chapter distinguishes the sources of hatred from the sources of contempt, then makes public esteem and popular goodwill the most practical defense against internal conspiracy.

The Roman emperors are not an exception to the rule but a harder test of it, because emperors had to manage soldiers as a third pressure alongside nobles and people. The chapter ends by extracting Severus for founding and Marcus for preserving.
